note: Literature confirms BRD4 alterations lead to atypical/milder CdLS where typical severe limb reduction deficiencies characteristic of classical NIPBL cases are reported to be largely absent or restricted to minor anomalies.

evidence.text: BRD4 alterations present with atypical or milder forms of Cornelia de Lange syndrome, in contrast to classic CdLS presentations.

source.title: Non-Classic Cornelia de Lange Syndrome Due to BRD4 Gene Alterations: A Literature Review
source.quote: Pathogenic variations in the NIPBL gene account for the majority of cases, but variations in several other genes, including BRD4, have been identified as causative factors for non-classic or milder forms of the syndrome.

evidence.text: Typical upper limb reduction defects seen in classic CdLS do not appear frequently in BRD4 patients, who primarily manifest with minor anomalies.
